chunks: As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿArzamī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

ʿAlī عليه السلام led the people in salat while not in a state of ritual purity, and it was the noon prayer. Then his caller went out and proclaimed: Surely Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام performed salat without ritual purity, so repeat, and let the one present convey it to the absent.

So this is an anomalous report, contrary to the hadiths, and that whose ruling is such is not to be acted upon. It also contains a further defect that undermines its soundness, namely that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام led the people in salat without wudu (ablution), whereas the indication of his ʿismah (infallibility) عليه السلام gives us certainty against that.

And Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh mentioned, saying: I heard a group of our shaykhs saying: There is no repetition upon them for anything in which he recited aloud, but they must repeat what he led them in of that in which he did not recite aloud.

key_terms.الْأَحَادِيثِ: the transmitted hadith reports used for legal and doctrinal evaluation
key_terms.خَبَرٌ شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report that conflicts with stronger transmissions
key_terms.طُهْرٍ: ritual purity required for valid salat
key_terms.عِصْمَتِهِ: his infallibility, indicating protection from such error
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on a report claiming Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام led salat without wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a report that Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام is said to have transmitted concerning Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام leading salat without ritual purity. The compiler rejects the report as anomalous and unsound because it contradicts other hadiths and conflicts with the Imam's ʿismah (infallibility). A secondary juristic view is then cited regarding whether followers must repeat prayers depending on whether the recitation was audible or silent.
